spec.title: Jobs, retries, backoff and wake confirmation

item.title: A job is one durable side effect
Attempts and escalations across the line
Rows and codes this domain owns

spec.purpose: Every side effect is a job: durable, idempotent, retried with backoff, confirmed when it is a wake, and dead-lettered with one note when it cannot be done. The bash belt lost wakes and retried nothing; this domain is the difference.

section.title: What the jobs domain decides

node.title: A wake is a job: sent through the executor, held while the seat's quiet window is open, confirmed by the seat's next record or its busy status, re-sent with backoff, and dead-lettered as a 500 note after the last attempt

Every action the scheduler performs is a job file with an idempotency key, so a restart resumes it, a crash never doubles it, and a verdict the executor could not deliver is discovered from the world before any retry

section.text: In: job specs from routing, policies, health and seats; verdicts from the executor; seat statuses and records for confirmation. Out: Run calls in order, state transitions, dead-letter notes.

section.title: A job is one durable side effect
section.text: One job is one executor verb with its arguments, about one record, with a key, a state, an attempt count, a next-due time and the keys it waits on. It is written before it is run and updated at every transition.

Kinds by origin: the primary, down and receipt of a routed record; the default and its wake from a policy; the notes and sweeps from health; the hold-and-release of seats. All go through the same store and runner.

The runner takes due, runnable jobs each tick and sends each to the executor on its own goroutine with the job's timeout; the tick loop never waits on a Run. Concurrency is bounded by the configured in-flight limit.
Jobs on one seat run one at a time, in record order, so two prompts never interleave in one pane and a bring-up finishes before its prompt.

section.title: The job store

text.source: AGENTS.md#Hard rule: dated entry files, one file per entry

section.text: One file per job under the state directory's jobs directory, named by the key, written to a temporary name and renamed, so a reader never sees a half-written job.
At start the store reads every file into memory indexes by state, record and seat; a transition updates the file first and the index second.
Done and dead jobs stay for the configured keep days so status and the parity report can read them, then are pruned by the health domain's housekeeping.

section.title: Idempotency and unknown outcomes
section.text: The key is the record id, a colon, the action, a colon, the target seat or file. A spec whose key already exists in the store is not created again; replaying a plan after a restart is a no-op.
Naturally idempotent verbs: seat-up on a live seat, seat-down twice, enqueue of a queued ticket. Not idempotent: prompt and record, which would double a line in a pane or a file in the log.
A Run whose outcome is unknown (timeout, connection lost mid-call, the executor restarted) is never retried blindly for prompt and record: the job enters discovery first.

Discovery, record job: intake saw a record from the scheduler's seat with the job's kind, ticket and note prefix after the attempt started: done. Prompt: the seat is busy or wrote a record after it: confirming. Else retry.

section.title: States
section.state: Created, or scheduled for a retry; runnable when its next-due time has passed and every job it waits on is satisfied.
Runnable but held by a domain with a reason: quiet, cap, absent, shared. Re-examined every tick; released into pending with next-due now.
A Run is in flight; the attempt count was incremented and the file written before the call.
The Run returned exit 0 for a prompt job; waiting for the seat's record or busy status inside the confirmation window.
Finished: exit 0, a handled final exit, or a confirmed wake. The last exit and the finish time are kept.
Given up after the last attempt, refused by the executor, or waiting on a job that died; the dead-letter note was written once.

section.title: Order between jobs
section.text: After lists the keys a job waits on: a plain key is satisfied by done only, a key with a trailing question mark by done or dead. The down of a routed record waits on the primary with the mark; the receipt waits on both without it.
A job waiting on a plain key whose job died is dead itself with reason after and the key, without running and without its own note: the primary's note already names the record.
Across records, jobs on one seat are serialised by record id; a later record's prompt to a seat waits for the earlier record's prompt to leave running.

section.title: Arguments and the prose fence
section.text: Arguments are a list of strings bound to the verb's argv template by position; no job ever carries a shell line. The executor refuses an argument holding a newline, so no record field can smuggle a second command or a second prompt.

An argument may carry the token that names an earlier job in After and is replaced at run time by the first line that job's Run printed: the id the event writer prints, which the wake after a policy default needs.
Note arguments are cut to the writer's limit before the Run; the writer's own refusal of a long note is then a bug, not a case.

section.title: Classifying a verdict
section.text: Exit 0: done, or confirming for a prompt. An exit code in the verb's final list: done with the exit kept, a handled result such as the seat script refusing a break glass it checked itself.
Refused by the executor (verb not in its table, argument with a newline, template error): dead at once with the refusal as the reason; this is a scheduler bug, not a condition of the world.
Any other exit code: a retry after backoff, until the verb's or the default maximum attempts. Timeout and connection loss: unknown, then discovery, then a retry when discovery finds nothing.
Exit 2 from a repository script is usage: a bug in the argument list, dead at once.

section.title: Backoff
section.text: Next due is now plus the base delay times the factor to the power of attempts already made, capped at the maximum delay, plus or minus the jitter fraction; every number is a configuration key, per verb where the verb table overrides.
The arithmetic is a pure function of attempt, the policy and a random fraction the caller passes; tests pass zero.
A restart keeps next-due from the file; a job due in the past runs on the first tick.

section.title: Dead letter
section.text: A primary job that dies writes the failure note of the routing domain and sets the ledger word to failed. Any other dead job writes one 500 note to the monitor naming the key, the attempts and the last reason. One note per job, ever.
A note job that dies writes no note: a log line at error level is its only trace, so a broken writer can never flood the log.
Dead jobs are listed by status with their reason until pruned; an operator who fixes the cause re-runs one with the retry subcommand, which resets attempts and next-due and nothing else.

section.title: Wake confirmation
section.text: A prompt job is confirmed when, after its Run started, the seat wrote any record on the job's ticket, or the seat was observed busy on any tick (the only signal for a fixed seat without a ticket). Confirmation ends the job as done.

The window is the role's acknowledgement seconds from the configuration; when it passes with no signal the job is re-sent as a new attempt with the same line, up to the wake maximum, then dead with a note saying wake unconfirmed.

A seat already busy with other work when the prompt lands reads as confirmed: the line sits in its input and is read at the next turn; the alternative, waiting for idle, would hold every wake behind every long command.
A wake handed to the inbox during a quiet window starts its window when the quiet file is gone.

section.title: The quiet window
section.text: Before a prompt runs the quiet verb asks whether the seat's quiet file exists. If so the job is held (reason quiet) and the inbox verb writes the wake line as one UTC-named file into the seat's inbox; the guard drains it after the resume.
The inbox write happens once per job: a held job whose line is in the inbox waits for the quiet file to go and then enters confirming, never a second prompt.
A seat with no state directory has no quiet file and is never quiet; the verb answers not quiet.

section.title: Attempts and escalations across the line
section.text: A seat's attempt on one ticket counts 1 to 3 in its own records; the third failure routes to the architect as a 423 instead of a fourth wake, and a 423 that reaches the architect twice becomes an owner decision card.
Job attempts and seat attempts are different counters: a job retries a side effect that did not happen; a seat attempt is a try that happened and failed. The scheduler never raises a seat's attempt.

section.title: Keys this domain reads
section.key: Attempts before dead, unless the verb table overrides.
Fraction of the delay added or removed at random.
How long done and dead jobs stay.
Confirmation window per role; every role in the roles directory must have a key.
Re-sends of an unconfirmed wake before it is dead.

section.title: Rows and codes this domain owns
section.owns-route: wake the worker with the record, down the tester.
escalate to the architect as 423, down the tester.
wake the worker with the record, down the reviewer.
escalate to the architect as 423, down the reviewer.
escalate to the architect as 423, the first time.
notify the owner through the interface agent, line decision, the second time.
section.owns-code: A gate failed with evidence and an attempt count; attempts below 3 go back to the worker.
A seat cannot continue, or a third failure: the architect once, the owner the second time.

case.expected: exit 0: putting the same spec twice yields one file; a plan replayed after a simulated restart creates nothing
exit 0: delays for attempts 1 to 5 equal base, base times factor, and so on, capped, with zero jitter
exit 0: exit 0 done, a final exit done with the code kept, refused dead, other exit retry, timeout discovery
exit 0: the down runs after a dead primary, the receipt never runs after a dead primary and is dead with reason after
exit 0: a prompt is confirming after exit 0 and done when the seat's record on the ticket lands inside the window
exit 0: no signal inside the window re-sends the same line, and after the maximum the job is dead with one 500 note
exit 0: with the quiet verb answering quiet the inbox verb is called once with the line and no prompt runs; when it answers not quiet the job enters confirming
exit 0: a timed-out record job is done when intake shows the record, and retried when it does not; a timed-out prompt is confirming when the seat is busy
exit 0: a dead primary writes the failure note once and the ledger word failed; a dead note job writes nothing

example.text: A worker wake is sent at 18:31:00; the worker's work.started lands at 18:31:40; the job is done and the log line says confirmed by record.
The executor socket drops during a receipt write; on the next tick intake lists a record.routed from the scheduler's seat for that record and the job is done without a second write.
Retrying a prompt the moment its Run timed out.
example.why: The line may already be in the pane; the seat would read it twice.

example.why: Attempts count tries that happened; a re-sent wake is the same try.
